market_context: The Nasdaq-100 fell 2.21% to 26,517.05 (QQQ -2.19% to $645.04) as a morning AI rally reversed once Anthropic (ANT) began trading, closing up 17% after a 34% opening pop; the S&P 500 dropped 2.02% to 7,175.83 for a sixth straight loss, the Dow lost 1,101 points, or 2.19%, to 49,097.06, and the VIX jumped 15.8% to 28.44.
market_cap_basis: Shares outstanding x 2026-11-19 close. Shares implied from Nasdaq market caps as of the 2026-10-29 close (watchlist market_cap_usd / 2026-10-29 close), so multi-class companies (e.g. GOOGL) reflect all share classes.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. Common Stock
stocks.reason: Shares sank after short-seller Hunterbrook Media published a report alleging that newer AMD firmware kept reaching blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems and that tighter U.S. export rules could hit AMD's China and Singapore business; Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a short position. AMD said the claims “misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships” and that it complies with U.S. export-control laws.

sources.title: AMD Has Its Own China Problem
AMD stock dives on short-seller report of alleged China exposure
AMD stock drops after Hunterbrook Media raises export control concerns

stocks.name: Palo Alto Networks Inc. Common Stock
stocks.reason: Shares rose after fiscal first-quarter results beat estimates (revenue $3.44 billion vs. $3.31 billion expected; adjusted EPS $1.05 vs. $0.97) and the company materially raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $14.52–$14.57 billion. It also announced a $4.5 billion all-stock deal to buy Applied Compute; Reuters said at least 20 brokerages raised price targets, with a median of $425.
